question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class agent-level config surface for operator-defined prompt/rules text, and what trust and precedence boundaries should it have?
rationale: This changes model-facing safety and operational instructions across sessions and can interact with Control UI/config mutation, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve Scoped Append Contract
options.body: Add `agents.defaults` plus per-agent append-only prompt/rules fields with explicit precedence, session coverage, docs, schema metadata, and security tests.

options.title: Reject New Core Prompt Config
options.body: Keep workspace bootstrap files, provider overlays, hooks, and channel prompt fields as the supported customization paths and document that agent-level prompt config is not planned.

options.title: Split Into Narrower Decisions
options.body: Handle raw includes through the existing include issue and hard enforcement through the response-gate issue before revisiting this softer prompt-rules surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Append Contract
recommendation.body: Add `agents.defaults` plus per-agent append-only prompt/rules fields with explicit precedence, session coverage, docs, schema metadata, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history on prompt/config boundaries and appears as the likely owner for deciding this model-facing config surface.
